question:
How many base \(10\) four-digit numbers, \(N=\underline{a\,b\,c\,d},\) satisfy all three of the following conditions?

(i) \(4{,}000\le N\lt6{,}000;\)

(ii) \(N\) is a multiple of \(5;\)

(iii) \(3\le b\lt c\le6.\)
solution:
Each condition restricts a particular part of the number. The range \(4000\le N<6000\) makes the thousands digit \(a\) either \(4\) or \(5\), giving two choices. A multiple of \(5\) must end in \(0\) or \(5\), giving two choices for \(d\).

For \(3\le b<c\le6\), the complete list of middle-digit pairs is
\[
(3,4),\ (3,5),\ (3,6),\ (4,5),\ (4,6),\ (5,6).
\]
There are six pairs: three with \(b=3\), two with \(b=4\), and one with \(b=5\). No other value of \(b\) allows a larger \(c\le6\).

Every choice of \(a\), one listed pair, and \(d\) satisfies all three conditions. Different choices produce different four-digit numbers, so none is counted twice. The total is
\[
2\cdot6\cdot2=24.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{24}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
